sentences: I measure the satellite's orbital position using ground-based radar and compare it with the predicted ephemeris.
I monitor the satellite's telemetry stream for voltage, current, and temperature readings from each subsystem.
I send a command to the satellite to switch its communication antenna to the backup transponder.
I check the satellite's solar panel output to ensure it matches the expected power generation for the current sun angle.
I record the satellite's battery charge level at regular intervals and log any deviation from the nominal discharge curve.
I adjust the thermal louvers on the satellite to keep the payload temperature within its operating range.
I command the satellite's reaction wheels to spin at specific rates to maintain its desired attitude.
I read the star tracker data to determine the satellite's orientation relative to the celestial sphere.
I calibrate the satellite's gyroscopes by comparing their readings with the star tracker during a known rotation.
I use the magnetometer to measure the Earth's magnetic field and derive the satellite's spin rate.
I point the satellite's high-gain antenna toward the ground station to establish a communication link for data transfer.
I downlink the stored science data when the satellite passes over the primary ground station.
I operate the satellite's imaging payload by sending commands to capture a series of photographs of the target area.
I verify the satellite's onboard computer memory usage and clear old log files to free up storage space.
I upload a software patch to the satellite to fix a minor bug in the attitude control algorithm.
I calculate the probability of collision with tracked debris and adjust the satellite's orbit if necessary.
I track the satellite's position relative to other objects in geostationary orbit to avoid interference.
I execute a small thruster burn to correct the satellite's drift and keep it within its designated orbital box.
I prepare the satellite for deorbit by commanding it to vent its remaining fuel and lower its orbit.
I review the satellite's end-of-life plan and update the ground station's contact schedule accordingly.
